result.title: Operator-Mismatch Contrastive Learning for World-Relative Trajectory Coherence
result.summary: World models are increasingly judged by how well they rank plausible futures, yet plausibility alone is the wrong target. The same scene can evolve under many latent rules, and a future that is smooth and physically valid under one rule can be incoherent under the rule actually in force. We formalize the resulting failure, operator-blindness, and show that it is systematically hidden by standard evaluation: a scorer can attain near-perfect generic ranking while separating current-world from other-world futures no better than chance. We introduce Operator-Mismatch Contrastive (OMC) learning, whose semantic hard negatives are valid-but-wrong-operator trajectories, and a matching protocol that measures world-relative coherence directly. On a controlled synthetic benchmark with in- and out-of-distribution operator parameters, across two trajectory-scoring backbones, and on feature-level external validation with CoPhy ballsCF, OMC raises operator-sensitive scoring far above a chance baseline that nonetheless achieves 0.99 generic top-1. We prove that the wrong-operator negative is necessary both for the protocol to detect the failure and for the objective to fix it, and position OMC as an auxiliary coherence signal (a trajectory-coherence scorer, not a generative model, planner, or control agent) that can be attached to existing world-model representations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对世界模型轨迹评分，形式化出「operator-blindness」失败：评分器在通用排序上近乎完美，却无法区分当前规则下连贯的未来与其他规则下连贯的未来；为此提出 Operator-Mismatch Contrastive 学习，用「有效但规则错误」的轨迹作语义硬负样本，并配套提出直接度量 world-relative coherence 的评测协议，在合成基准与 CoPhy ballsCF 特征级验证上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其硬负样本构造与「当前世界 vs 其他世界」判别协议，可能与 LVR 中多 latent 假设的筛选与评价、排除看似合理却错误的内部状态相关，可供核查；论文本身不涉及视觉语言推理，属较远领域的启发线索。
